**Detail bug report:** [View on Detail](https://app.detail.dev/org_d38a878f-9df9-4c4b-a96a-f5180b860085/bugs/bug_e0ed81b4-68c0-42bd-baf2-beffc06e1a09)

## Bug

`CoreComponent.unstyled: Var[bool]` lets users opt out of a component's default Tailwind classes — but only `CoreComponent.set_class_name` ever consulted the prop. Many `create()` methods built `class_name` directly with `cn(defaults, custom_classes)` and forwarded `**props` to `super().create(...)` without popping `unstyled`. The prop was then stripped from the rendered output by `_exclude_props`, so users got a fully-styled component with no error and no visible trace that the prop was ignored. The bug was inconsistent: e.g. `TabsTrigger` honored `unstyled` while `TabsRoot`/`TabsList`/`TabsContent` ignored it; `NativeSelectOptionComponent` honored it while `NativeSelectComponent` did not.

Affected: `Button`, `TabsRoot`/`TabsList`/`TabsContent`, `AvatarRoot`/`AvatarFallback`/`AvatarBadge`/`AvatarGroup`/`AvatarGroupCount`, `NativeSelectComponent` (both `<select>` and wrapper `<div>`), `BadgeComponent`, all six `Frame*` components, `InputComponent`.

Closes #106

## Fix

Routed every previously-bypassing `create()` through `CoreComponent.set_class_name(default_class, props)` — the same mechanism the already-conforming components (`NativeSelectOptionComponent`, `TableHeader`, `DialogHeader`, `CardRoot`, etc.) already use. `set_class_name` pops `unstyled` and either:
- `unstyled=True` → renders only the user's `class_name` (defaults stripped),
- `unstyled=False` (or omitted) → renders `cn(defaults, user_class_name)` (existing behavior preserved).

For `NativeSelectComponent`, which builds both a `<select>` and a wrapper `<div>` in one `create()`, `unstyled` is popped once and applied to both elements' default-class merge; the dropdown chevron's hardcoded `ClassNames.ICON` is left intact since `unstyled` is about the select, not its decorative icon. `components/ui/input.py` no longer imports `cn` (the one `cn(...)` call became `set_class_name`), so the unused import was dropped.

The regenerated `assets/docs/components/*.md` reflect the source changes verbatim (the docs engine embeds component source on each component's "Source Code" card). The CI "Generate & Verify Docs and Social Cards" gate runs `scripts/generate_markdown.py` and checks `git diff --exit-code assets/docs`, so the regenerated docs are committed alongside the source fix.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest tests/` — 567 pass (473 pre-existing + 94 new in `tests/test_unstyled.py`). New regression tests cover per component: default merge with user class, `unstyled=False` ≡ default, `unstyled=True` strips defaults but keeps user class, `unstyled=True` with no user class is blank, and `unstyled` does not leak into `custom_attrs`. `NativeSelectOptionComponent` is included as an already-conforming control.
- `tests/test_unstyled.py` also adds dedicated cases for `NativeSelectComponent`'s dual-element behavior: unstyled strips defaults on both the `<select>` and the wrapper div, the user's `class_name`/`wrapper_class_name` don't bleed across elements, and the chevron icon keeps its positioning classes.
- `uv run ruff check` + `uv run ruff format --check` (both default and `.trunk/configs/ruff.toml`) — clean on all 9 touched files.
- `trunk check --no-fix <touched files>` — "No new issues" (47 pre-existing in those files, none introduced by the fix; the Trunk CLI and the `pyrefly`/`tach` tools had to be installed first via `curl -sSfL https://get.trunk.io/cli-install | bash` and `uv tool install pyrefly tach`).
- `uv run tach check` — "All modules validated!"
- `uv run pyrefly check` (strict) — pyrefly-neutral: the committed `pyrefly.toml` already reports 413 pre-existing errors on the pristine baseline, and the fix leaves that count unchanged (no new errors; `tests/test_unstyled.py` itself reports 0).
- `uv run python scripts/generate_markdown.py` + `git diff --exit-code assets/docs` — only the 10 component docs that embed the modified source change (all diffs are verbatim copies of the new `create()` bodies, not behavioral doc changes). The doc/asset/card-count test suite (`test_generated_assets.py`, `test_docs_error.py`, `test_components_card_counts.py` — 348 tests) passes both before and after regeneration.
- Bug-report reproduction scripts were re-run: every previously-bypassing component now produces a stripped `class_name` with `unstyled=True`, and `NativeSelectComponent` produces only the user's `class_name` on the `<select>` and only the user's `wrapper_class_name` on the wrapper. Both scripts print the expected success messages.

from typing import Any

from reflex.components.component import Component
from reflex.utils.imports import ImportVar
from reflex.vars import FunctionVar, Var
from reflex.vars.base import VarData

PACKAGE_CN = "clsx-for-tailwind@1.0.0"
CN = Var(
    "cn",
    _var_data=VarData(
        imports={
            PACKAGE_CN: ImportVar(tag="cn"),
        },
    ),
).to(FunctionVar)


class CoreComponent(Component):
    unstyled: Var[bool]

    @classmethod
    def set_class_name(
        cls,
        default_class_name: str | Var[str],
        props: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:

        if "render_" in props:
            return

        props_class_name = props.get("class_name", "")

        if props.pop("unstyled", False):
            props["class_name"] = props_class_name
            return

        props["class_name"] = cn(default_class_name, props_class_name)

    def _exclude_props(self) -> list[str]:
        return [
            *super()._exclude_props(),
            "unstyled",
        ]


def cn(*classes: Var | str | tuple | list | None) -> Var:
    return CN.call(*classes).to(str)

"""Regression tests for the ``unstyled`` prop across CoreComponent subclasses.

Background: ``CoreComponent`` in ``components/core/core.py`` declares
``unstyled: Var[bool]``. When ``True``, the component should strip its own
default Tailwind classes and render only user-supplied ``class_name``. The
mechanism lives in ``CoreComponent.set_class_name``: any ``create()`` that
routes its ``class_name`` through ``set_class_name`` gets the behavior for
free; ``create()`` methods that build ``class_name`` directly with ``cn(...)``
and pass ``**props`` through to ``super().create(...)`` previously bypassed
``set_class_name`` and silently ignored ``unstyled``.

This file guards against that regression by asserting, for every
``CoreComponent`` whose ``create()`` previously bypassed ``set_class_name``:

  1. By default (``unstyled`` not set) the component's default classes are
     applied alongside any user-supplied ``class_name``.
  2. With ``unstyled=True`` and user ``class_name`` set, the rendered
     ``class_name`` contains ONLY the user-supplied classes; no component
     default class survives.
  3. With ``unstyled=True`` and no user ``class_name``, the component
     renders with an empty/blank ``class_name`` (no defaults leak).
  4. With ``unstyled=True`` no ``unstyled`` attribute leaks into the
     component's rendered custom_attrs (it remains excluded from the DOM).

It also re-runs the same checks against ``NativeSelectOptionComponent`` as a
control case: that component already routed through ``set_class_name`` before
this fix, so its behavior must not regress.

For ``NativeSelectComponent``, which renders both a ``<select>`` element and
a wrapper ``<div>`` from a single ``create()`` call, the same set of
guarantees is checked against BOTH the inner ``<select>`` (using the user's
``class_name``) and the outer wrapper (using ``wrapper_class_name``).

"""``unstyled`` regression tests for InputGroup components bypassing set_class_name."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from components.ui.input_group import (
    ClassNames,
    InputGroupButton,
    InputGroupInput,
    InputGroupTextarea,
)

CASES = [
    (InputGroupButton, "shadow-none"),
    (InputGroupInput, ClassNames.CONTROL_INPUT.split()[0]),
    (InputGroupTextarea, ClassNames.CONTROL_TEXTAREA.split()[0]),
]


def _class_name(component: object) -> str:
    return str(component.class_name)  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("cls", "default"), CASES)
def test_defaults_merged(cls: type, default: str) -> None:
    out = _class_name(cls.create(class_name="user-x"))
    assert default in out
    assert "user-x" in out


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("cls", "default"), CASES)
def test_unstyled_strips_defaults(cls: type, default: str) -> None:
    out = _class_name(cls.create(class_name="user-x", unstyled=True))
    assert "user-x" in out
    assert default not in out
